readme: The declared branch-protection contract for `main`. GitHub owns the live setting;
this file is the committed claim about it, and src/__tests__/required-checks-contract.test.ts
holds that claim to the workflows in this repository so a required context can never name
The failure this exists to prevent: a required context whose name matches no check any PR
posts wedges EVERY pull request forever, and nothing in the repo objects. The near miss shape
is a job in a workflow with a `paths:` filter (security-audit.yml) or one that never runs on
pull_request at all (deploy-pages.yml, dev-agent-runner.yml) - those report SKIPPED or nothing.

required.why: The consolidated Quality Gate: lint, typecheck, build, `npm audit --audit-level=high`, and the full vitest suite. The name is the legacy pre-consolidation one, kept because it is the protected context; ci.yml's last step posts it from the quality-gate job so the required name and the real gate are the same run.

The Web Vitals regression gate (v0.18, PR #136), shipped deliberately non-required per WEB_VITALS_BASELINE.md D4 so it could earn requiredness through observed stability. Evidence at promotion: 58 runs of lighthouse.yml since 2026-08-01, exactly 1 failure, and that one was on the PR branch that introduced the workflow, BEFORE it merged (run 30707624249). 55 consecutive green runs post-merge across 7 days, 28 of them on main pushes. Zero noise-only reds, so the `numberOfRuns: 5` tightening the backlog held in reserve was never needed.

observational.why: Playwright smoke journeys over the real static export (v0.16, PR #126). Runs unfiltered on every PR, so it is eligible for promotion. DECISION 2026-08-18 (PR #190): the evidence bar lighthouse set IS MET - the post-merge window (since #126 merged 2026-07-27T01:54Z, 22 days) holds 144 runs of e2e.yml with ZERO failures: 139 success plus 5 cancelled, every cancellation a supersession by the workflow's own cancel-in-progress concurrency group (each has a green run on the same branch within a minute), 64 main-push runs all green. The only failure in the workflow's life (run 30230736206) was on the PR branch that introduced it, BEFORE it merged - the identical shape to lighthouse's one red at its promotion. PROMOTION IS DECIDED AND PENDING EXECUTION: the live PATCH of required_status_checks was denied by the session permission classifier (2026-08-18, tried twice), and this file never claims a protection GitHub does not enforce. To execute: run the readme's PATCH command with contexts lint-and-build, lighthouse, e2e and strict=true, then move this entry to required[] with requiredSince set to that day.

The job that DOES the work behind the required `lint-and-build` status. Not itself required, so that the protected name stays a single stable string while the job behind it is free to be renamed or split.

The daily advisory detector. Its pull_request trigger is path-filtered to the workflow file itself, so most PRs never receive this check. It can therefore NEVER be a required context - requiring it would block every PR that does not touch security-audit.yml. Its gate value is already required: ci.yml runs the identical `npm audit --audit-level=high`, and workflow-audit-parity.test.ts holds the two to the same threshold.

actions/dependency-review-action@v5.0.0 at `fail-on-severity: high` (2026-08-12, PR #183). DECISION, so a later sweep does not re-file it: it ships OBSERVATIONAL on purpose, the same route lighthouse.yml took before PR #161 promoted it on 58 observed runs. THE ACCEPTED RISK, stated plainly: a pull request that adds a dependency with a HIGH GitHub advisory shows a RED `dependency-review` check and is still mergeable, and nothing here will stop it. What makes that acceptable is not that the risk is small but that it is COVERED TWICE: ci.yml's `npm audit --audit-level=high` resolves the same tree and IS required, so the only gap this leaves is an advisory GitHub's database carries and the npm registry's does not yet. If that overlap ever went away - the audit step scoped to `--omit=dev`, or moved out of the required job - this decision flips to required immediately, because the advisory check would then be the only one. PROMOTE IT when the evidence lighthouse produced exists here too: at least 30 runs of dependency-review.yml with no failure that was not a real dependency finding, read from `gh run list --workflow dependency-review.yml`. Promotion edits this entry, `.github/required-checks.json`'s required[] array, and the live branch protection in one PR.

Posted by the GitGuardian GitHub App, not by any workflow in this repository. Left observational because nothing committed here can prove it posts on every PR, which is the exact property a required context needs. `gh pr checks --watch` also does not wait for a check run that has not appeared yet (L-039), so an app-posted required context is the one that strands a merge.
